# Full Data Management Checklist

## Planning

- [ ] Does your data management plan include naming conventions, folder organisation, and documentation? 
- [ ] Have you defined and assigned roles and responsibilities identifying who will collect, manage, and archive the data?
- [ ] Has everyone agreed to how they will be provided appropriate attribution in all project outputs?  
- [ ] Have you decided how data will be stored, backed up, and accessed throughout the project lifecycle?  
- [ ] Do you have plans for long-term sharing and stewardship once the project is complete? 
- [ ] Have you set a date (or milestone) for reviewing your plans?

## Creating

- [ ] Are all administrative requirements completed before planning data collection, e.g. ethics approval, risk assessment?
- [ ] Have you agreed upon a robust data collection protocol that takes into consideration the specific place and time where you will be collecting your data?
- [ ] Have you developed a collection template for all researchers conducting data collection?
- [ ] Have you set up a secure online folder to store backups of collected data?
- [ ] Are there any critical issues that were noted during data collection that need to be addressed before collating your data into a raw dataset? If yes, have you dealt with these?
- [ ] Have you decided on a format for your raw dataset?
- [ ] Have you assigned unique IDs to each observation, avoiding any special characters in the IDs?
- [ ] Have you created backups of your raw dataset?

## Processing

- [ ] Are you using a data format that maintains its accessibility in the long term?
- [ ] Are you using a widely recognised data format to ensure interoperability of your dataset?
- [ ] Have you checked that you haven’t lost or corrupted any data during processing?
- [ ] Is the main version of your file (used for research and sharing) easily identifiable?
- [ ] Is your processing code well organised and version controlled?
- [ ] Have you checked your data for validity and accuracy?
- [ ] Have you cleaned your data with all steps clearly documented?

## Documenting

- [ ] Have you included a README file that includes all the recommended information?
- [ ] Have you created a data dictionary, or included this information in your README?
- [ ] Have you followed an established metadata standard that matches the type of data you are collecting (where appropriate)?
- [ ] Have you included enough documentation that others can understand and reuse the data? Get a colleague who is not familiar with the project to check. 

## Preserving

- [ ] Is the main copy of the data stored in a shared location and not tied to a single individual’s account? 
- [ ] Are your data backed up using a 3-2-1 approach (three copies, two locations, one offsite)? 
- [ ] Have you checked institutional policies on cloud and third-party storage, especially for sensitive data? 
- [ ] Are your backups automated where possible? Have you tested to confirm that they can be restored? 
- [ ] Have you identified files required for long-term retention (including raw data, processed datasets, and documentation)? 
- [ ] Is there a plan for maintaining access to data when team members leave or move institutions? 
- [ ] Have you reviewed requirements from funders and target journals for data preservation and repository deposition?

## Sharing 

- [ ] Have you checked for a domain-specific repository for your data type?
- [ ] Have you checked if your funder requires a specific repository?
- [ ] Have you attached a licence to your dataset? 
- [ ] Have you deposited your data in a repository, rather than as Supplemental Information? 
- [ ] If you are sharing code, have you created a permanent, citable snapshot with a DOI via Zenodo or equivalent, not solely relying on version control platforms such as GitHub?
- [ ] Does your data contain sensitive information, such as precise locations of endangered species or personal data from human participants? If so, have you removed or protected it before deposit?

:::
